_comment_alertSuppress: A listing marked Cold is not being actively pushed, so it should not raise alerts. Items whose 'temperature' column reads one of these values are excluded from every attention panel and its counts: what to touch next, deadlines, approval queue, stalled, going cold, and the tab badges. They stay in the capacity chart and hygiene, because the work is still assigned and pretending otherwise would understate someone's load.
_comment_statusStamp: Labels whose moment-of-application is worth showing. For these, the server reads the status column's activity log and stamps each item with when the label was set, so a card can say 'Proofs Sent' AND when. lookbackDays bounds that history query; a label applied longer ago than this shows without a time rather than with a wrong one.
_comment_stackAdapt: A second data source, and the only one that is not monday: StackAdapt paid-media campaigns, shown only in the Mac rail. What matters is the EDGE of a flight -- a campaign about to go dark needs a renewal decision, one that just went dark needs a wrap report -- so only campaigns whose end date falls inside a narrow window either side of today are listed. advertiserIds is a hard allowlist, not a preference: the account carries other advertisers and none of them are ours. Note 94831 (Aperture) is the advertiser asked for; the LPT Realty advertiser 73763 holds the '...Luxury Orders' listing campaigns, so add "73763" here to pick those up too. The API's own endedAfter filter was tested and does NOT hard-filter (it returns null and years-old end dates), so the window is computed in derive.js from each campaign's own UTC offset and never delegated. A campaign can have several flights: its effective end is the latest one, and a campaign with ANY open-ended flight counts as having no end at all rather than being reported finished. Set enabled false, or delete this block, and the section disappears with no extra API call. The token lives in web/.env as STACKADAPT_API_TOKEN or as a Worker secret; without it the section is simply absent and nothing else changes.

stackAdapt._comment_campaignUrlTemplate: Clicking a campaign in the rail opens it in StackAdapt. There is NO per-campaign page: the platform's campaign view is a filtered list, so the link passes the campaign name in the search param and the board opens filtered to it. Pattern confirmed from a real address bar, not guessed -- an earlier guess at app.stackadapt.com had no DNS record at all and produced dead links. {name} is URL-encoded; {id} is also available but the UI's URLs never use it. Their site is a single-page app that answers 200 for any path, so a wrong path cannot be detected by probing -- only by clicking. Set to null to make rows unclickable.

_comment_stepNaming: Items whose name opens with a number and a bracket -- '1) captions drafts' -- are numbered steps within a piece of work, not projects of their own. They stay visible everywhere they already appear, but they are left out of the project counts: the header total, each person's capacity total, and the parent's subtask count.
_comment_lanes: Every status label on every board maps to exactly one lane. Lanes drive all the math. Unknown labels default to 'active'.
_comment_lanemeta: Display order, label and severity role for each lane.
_comment_scopes: The header toggle. Each board declares a scope; 'both' is the union. Order here is the order of the buttons.
_comment_rndTag: Items whose request-type column carries this value belong to the R&D scope ONLY: they are excluded from design/aperture/both entirely, and the R&D view is a plain list grouped by assignee.

boards._comment: 177 listing orders. 'Design' (status7) is the column that matters creatively — the others track Billboard/Magazine/Mailer separately. There is NO due-date column on this board, so date is intentionally null: deadline panels stay empty rather than inventing a deadline out of 'Proofs Sent'. 'temperature' is the Cold/Warm/Hot column.

boards._why: Orders (18404619594) is Brittany's board, not design team work. Its items were inflating the overdue count and putting non-designers in the capacity chart. Delete this block to drop it for good, or remove _disabled to bring it back.

_comment_you: Your monday user id. Items where you are the approver or assignee get an extra nudge in the focus ranking.
_comment_personColors: Assignee colour slots 1-5. Pinned by name on purpose: if slots were assigned by sort order, adding a designer whose name sorts early would repaint everyone else's rows. Colour must follow the person, not their position. Anyone not listed here takes the next free slot alphabetically; past slot 5 they render neutral grey. Identity is always carried by the initials and name on the card — the colour is a scanning aid, because no 5-hue set can be told apart reliably enough to carry identity alone.
